vulnerability.title: Symfony UrlGenerator dot-segment encoding skips every other chained ../ or ./ segment, so generated URLs collapse off-route under RFC 3986 normalization

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.4.53 doGenerate() splits the path on / and percent-encodes every "." and ".." segment individually; the strtr plus trailing fixup is gone

fix_commits.message: [Routing] Fix dot-segment encoding for chained "../" and "./" in generated URLs

vulnerability.category_l2: Dot-segment encoding defect in URL generation; generated URL normalizes to a different path (route confusion / off-route)

critical_operation.description: doGenerate() encodes "." and ".." path segments so a generated URL still resolves to its route after RFC 3986 §5.2.4 dot-segment removal. The encoding uses two strtr() replacements, "/../" -> "/%2E%2E/" and "/./" -> "/%2E/". strtr() consumes the trailing slash of each match, so in a chained sequence such as "../../.." the slash that ends one match is the slash that would start the next; every other segment is left as a literal "." or "..". A URL built from an attacker-controlled route parameter therefore contains unencoded dot segments that strict RFC 3986 consumers (routers, reverse proxies, HTTP clients) remove before percent-decoding, so the URL collapses to a different path than the route intended. The trailing-segment fixup only covers the last segment. The 5.4.53 fix splits the path on / and encodes every dot segment.

entry_point.description: An application generates a URL from a route whose parameter is attacker-influenced, e.g. linking to a user-supplied path or a return URL.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read UrlGenerator::doGenerate() at v5.4.45 and confirm the two strtr rules plus terminal fixup, and that chained dot segments are skipped.
An independent reviewer must confirm 4b63c3a3 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.53, and that it encodes every segment.

No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No URL was generated and no RFC 3986 normalization was executed; the collapse is established statically from the strtr semantics and the fix tests.
Only the 5.4 branch was inspected; 6.4.41, 7.4.13 and 8.0.13 were not diffed.
The CNA and OSV CVSS 4.0 vectors disagree on UI and VI; both remain Medium.
open_questions: The precise downstream impact depends on the consuming router/proxy; no specific deployment was tested.
Whether non-path uses of generate() (host/fragment) are affected was not analysed.
